aiOverview.content: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations, often forming tumors or spreading via the bloodstream/lymph system. Diagnosis involves physical exams, imaging, and lab tests, while treatments typically include surgery, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. Prevention focuses on reducing risk factors like smoking, poor diet, and alcohol.Key Aspects of CancerDefinition & Types: Cancer occurs when abnormal cells divide without control, invading nearby tissues. Main types include carcinomas (skin/tissue lining), sarcomas (bone/connective tissue), and leukemia/lymphoma (blood/immune system).Causes & Risks: Cancer results from gene alterations (DNA changes) that can be inherited or caused by environmental exposures, such as tobacco (leading cause), UV radiation, and certain infections.Diagnosis Methods: Early detection is crucial, often found through physical exams, imaging tests (CT, MRI), and laboratory tests, such as blood, urine, or tumor marker tests.Treatment Options: Common treatments include surgery to remove tumors, radiation therapy, chemotherapy (using drugs to kill cells), and newer methods like immunotherapy, which boosts the body's natural defenses.Latest Advancements & Trends: Research is focusing on targeted therapies that attack specific genetic changes, personalized immunotherapies (like CAR-T cell therapy), and improving early detection methods.Global Burden & PreventionStatistics: In 2022, there were roughly 20 million new cases and 9.7 million deaths worldwide. By 2050, cases are expected to reach 33 million per year.Prevention: Up to 50% of cancer deaths are preventable, primarily by avoiding tobacco, maintaining a healthy weight, and limiting alcohol.
